exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse)
to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: прийти́ — to come (to), to arrive (at); приня́ть — to take; прие́хать — to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse); приходи́ть — to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity).
**приеду** — прие́хать (perfective): to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse); (past tense, plural only) to hit rock bottom. Wiktionary: при- + е́хать.
exercises.context: Which prefix? The English says which word it is.

pairs: to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere)
to order, to command, to give orders, to direct
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: принести́ — to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); приказа́ть — to order, to command, to give orders, to direct; принима́ть — to take; присла́ть — to send (here, to this place).

**принёс** — принести́ (perfective): to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear; to offer (apologies, thanks, etc.). Wiktionary: при- + нести́.
exercises.context: Which prefix? The English says which word it is.
